editorial:
If you enjoy dark comedies that poke fun at smart people making dumb choices, this one is right up your alley. The story follows a worn-out philosophy professor who arrives at a small college campus feeling completely empty inside. He drinks too much, talks in circles, and seems to have given up. Things shift when he starts spending time with a bright, curious student who sees something in him that he cannot see himself. Their connection gives him a strange new spark, and suddenly he feels alive again.

Joaquin Phoenix carries the film with a messy, believable performance that makes you feel his sadness and confusion. Emma Stone is charming and sharp as the student pulled into his world. The pacing is slow and talky, so if you want action, this is not for you. The humor is subtle and sometimes uncomfortable, which is part of the fun. You should watch it if you like character-driven stories with a dark edge. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Abe carries out his plan to poison the judge and feels reborn. But Jill figures out what he did and confronts him. To keep his secret, Abe tries to push Jill into an open elevator shaft. She steps aside at the last second, and Abe tumbles down the shaft to his death. Jill walks away, finally free of him, and the story ends on a quiet, bittersweet note.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark character studies and dry humor.
